text:
Sheldon Dries is the hometown story on a Red Wings roster that could use one. The 32-year-old from Macomb, Michigan went undrafted, built a career mostly in the AHL, and has now played 15 games for Detroit at about ten minutes a night, after earlier NHL stints with Colorado and Vancouver.

The scoring hasn't come. He has one assist and no goals, on chances that would usually produce one or two (1.51 expected goals). His rate of chances is close to typical for a depth forward, so the zero looks more like bad luck than a lack of looks.

The harder part is territory. Detroit has 47.2% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on at five on five, and has been outshot in those minutes. He's physical (33 hits in 15 games) and quick, with a top speed in the 73rd percentile in NHL Edge tracking. On a fourth line, that energy is the job; his first goal of the season, in front of the home crowd he grew up in, would be a nice bonus.
